narrative: An attacker at 203.0.113.150 abused a path-traversal/upload flaw in upload.php (web_access.jsonl:2-3) to drop a PHP webshell at /var/www/html/uploads/media.php (filemod.csv:1) and executed commands through it (web_access.jsonl:4). They spawned a bash reverse shell to 203.0.113.150:4444 (linux_proc.jsonl:2, bash_history.csv:1, netflow.csv:1), downloaded an enumeration script (bash_history.csv:2), escalated privileges via a SUID-find sudo misconfig (linux_proc.jsonl:4, auth_log.jsonl:4), installed a root cron job /usr/local/sbin/.update for persistence (cron.csv:1, bash_history.csv:4), and pivoted over SSH to db01 with a stolen key (linux_proc.jsonl:5, auth_log.jsonl:5, netflow.csv:3). Blast radius: web01, db01, and the www-data -> root escalation.
decoy: Just before the alert, an internet SSH brute-force from 198.51.100.66 hit root and admin (auth_log.jsonl:1-3). It looks like the entry vector but every attempt is a Failed password with no Accepted login, and the IP is rated benign (threat_intel.csv:3). Googlebot crawler traffic (web_access.jsonl:6-7) is also benign. A correct agent must self-correct from the SSH brute-force theory to the web-application compromise.
root_cause: A vulnerable upload.php allowed a PHP webshell that gave command execution, leading to a reverse shell, privilege escalation, cron persistence, and an SSH pivot to db01.

expected_findings.label: Web shell deployed to web root

expected_decoy_rejections.claim: The SSH brute-force from 198.51.100.66 is the entry vector
expected_decoy_rejections.must_reject_because: all SSH attempts are Failed password with no Accepted login and the IP is rated benign (threat_intel.csv:3)
